applyTo: "src/components/**/*.astro,src/layouts/**/*.astro,src/pages/**/*.astro"

# Ejected Proxy Customization Guide

## Understanding Proxy Wrappers

When you run `npx crss eject <target>`, the CLI creates a proxy wrapper
file in your project. This proxy imports the core component and passes
through all props and slots. You customize by uncommenting slot blocks
and adding your own content.

## File Structure

Each proxy has three sections:

### 1. Managed Import Block

```astro
---
/*
 * @start-eject-import
 */
import CoreBaseLayout from '@community-rss/core/layouts/BaseLayout.astro';
import AuthButton from '@community-rss/core/components/AuthButton.astro';

interface Props {
  title: string;
}

const props = Astro.props;
/*
 * @end-eject-import
 */
---
```

**Important:** The block between `@start-eject-import` and
`@end-eject-import` is regenerated on re-eject. Do not place custom
imports inside it — they will be lost. Place your custom imports
**after** the `@end-eject-import` marker:

```astro
/*
 * @end-eject-import
 */
import MyCustomComponent from '../components/MyCustomComponent.astro';
---
```

### 2. Slot Override Blocks

Each named slot appears as a commented block:

```astro
{/* =========================================
  SLOT: header
  Replace the default header/nav bar.
  =========================================
*/}

{/* <Fragment slot="header">
  <header class="crss-header">...</header>
</Fragment> */}
```

To activate a slot override, **uncomment** the `<Fragment>` block and
replace its content:

```astro
{/* =========================================
  SLOT: header
  Replace the default header/nav bar.
  =========================================
*/}

<Fragment slot="header">
  <header class="my-custom-header">
    <nav>My Custom Navigation</nav>
  </header>
</Fragment>
```

### 3. Style Block

Add your custom CSS at the bottom:

```astro
<style>
  .my-custom-header {
    background: var(--crss-sys-color-primary);
  }
</style>
```

## Re-ejecting (Upgrading)

When the framework updates and adds new slots or changes defaults, run
the eject command again without `--force`:

```bash
npx crss eject components/FeedCard
```

This will:
- **Preserve** your active slot overrides (uncommented `<Fragment>` blocks)
- **Preserve** your custom `<style>` content
- **Preserve** your custom imports (outside the managed block)
- **Update** the managed import block with any new imports/types
- **Add** commented blocks for any new slots added by the framework
- **Remove** orphan overrides for slots that no longer exist

### Force Eject

To completely reset a proxy to the fresh default (discarding all
customizations):

```bash
npx crss eject components/FeedCard --force
```

## Tips

1. The comment block above each slot shows the **current core default**.
   Compare it to your override to see if the core has changed.

2. Only uncomment the slots you actually want to customize. Fewer
   overrides mean easier upgrades.

3. Use CSS custom properties (`--crss-*` tokens) in your style overrides
   for consistency with the framework's design system.

4. If you see a `SLOT:` marker in a comment, the proxy was generated by
   the eject CLI — it's safe to re-eject.
